title: Nephi yields the judgment-seat
summary: Nephi hands the judgment-seat to Cezoram. The people’s laws and governments are corrupted, and they are ripening for destruction.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi delivered up the judgment-seat to Cezoram.
Those choosing evil outnumbered those choosing good, and the laws had become corrupted.
The people could not be governed by law or justice without destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Cezoram are together as the judgment-seat is handed over.
unspecified_visual_details: The judgment-seat’s appearance and the place of the transfer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unmentioned public ceremony or additional participants.

title: Nephi and Lehi choose to preach
summary: Weary of the people’s iniquity, Nephi gives up the judgment-seat and commits himself to preaching for the rest of his days. Lehi does likewise, remembering their father Helaman’s words.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi yielded up the judgment-seat and took it upon himself to preach the word of God for the rest of his days; his brother Lehi did so too.
They remembered the words their father Helaman spoke to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Lehi may be shown together, recalling their father’s teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the brothers are speaking together or separately, and the location.

narration.text: they remembered the words which their father Helaman spake unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Helaman’s words are recalled in the following scenes; these verses do not place him physically present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Helaman speaking in person.

title: Helaman’s counsel: remember good examples
summary: Helaman counsels his sons to keep God’s commandments, declare his words, remember the good works of their namesakes, and do good themselves.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman said he had given his sons the names of their first parents who came from Jerusalem, so they would remember their names and good works.
Helaman urged his sons to do good as their first parents had done.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The counsel can be conveyed as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and whether Helaman’s sons are shown listening.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, my sons, I desire that ye should remember to keep the commandments of God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman (quoted counsel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is remembered teaching, not a newly occurring conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the first parents as present.

title: Helaman’s counsel: treasure in heaven
summary: Helaman tells his sons not to do good for boasting, but to seek eternal life, and reminds them that salvation comes through Jesus Christ’s atoning blood.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman urged his sons to do good without boasting and to seek eternal life.
Helaman cited King Benjamin’s words that salvation comes only through Jesus Christ’s atoning blood, and that Christ would come to redeem the world.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and whether listeners are visible.

spoken_dialogue.text: O remember, remember, my sons, the words which king Benjamin spake unto his people;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman (quoted counsel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The coming of Jesus Christ is recalled teaching, not a present visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict King Benjamin or Jesus Christ as physically present.

title: Helaman’s counsel: redemption from sin
summary: Helaman recalls Amulek’s teaching to Zeezrom that the Lord redeems people from their sins, not in their sins, and that repentance leads to the Redeemer’s salvation.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman recalled Amulek’s teaching to Zeezrom in Ammonihah that the Lord would redeem people from their sins, not in their sins.
The Redeemer has power from the Father to redeem people through repentance; angels declare the conditions of repentance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be conveyed as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and whether listeners are visible.

spoken_dialogue.text: he should not come to redeem them in their sins, but to redeem them from their sins.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman (quoted counsel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The mention of angels is part of Helaman’s teaching, not a narrated angelic appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Amulek’s earlier conversation with Zeezrom as a present event.

title: Helaman’s counsel: build on the rock
summary: Helaman tells his sons to build upon Christ, the sure foundation, so that the devil’s storms cannot bring them down. Helaman taught them many other things as well.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman taught his sons to build their foundation on Christ, the Son of God, so they could not fall.
Helaman taught his sons many things, both written and unwritten.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The counsel can be presented as off-screen speech; the rock and storm language may be treated as figurative teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and whether listeners are visible.

spoken_dialogue.text: it is upon the rock of our Redeemer, who is Christ, the Son of God, that ye must build your foundation;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman (quoted counsel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rock, winds, shafts, hail, and storm are figures within the teaching, not a narrated physical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal supernatural storm or a visible Christ.

title: Nephi and Lehi begin preaching
summary: Remembering Helaman’s words, Nephi and Lehi go out to teach among the people of Nephi, starting at Bountiful and then going to Gid and Mulek.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi remembered Helaman’s words, kept God’s commandments, and began teaching at Bountiful.
They went from Bountiful to Gid, then from Gid to Mulek.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The brothers travel between the named cities.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the cities and route between them.

narration.text: they went forth, keeping the commandments of God, to teach the word of God

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific sermons or encounters in these cities.

title: Teaching through the lands
summary: Nephi and Lehi travel among the people of Nephi in the land southward and into Zarahemla among the Lamanites. Dissenters confess their sins, are baptized, and return to the Nephites to repair their wrongs.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi went from city to city among the people of Nephi in the land southward, then into Zarahemla among the Lamanites.
Their preaching confounded many dissenters, who confessed their sins, were baptized unto repentance, and returned to the Nephites to try to repair their wrongs.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The conversions and baptisms follow the preaching, but the verse does not specify where each took place.
unspecified_visual_details: The location of each confession and baptism, and the manner of making restitution.

narration.text: they came forth and did confess their sins

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The summary reports outcomes without staging the whole sequence as one simultaneous moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the dissenters’ identities or specific acts of restitution.

title: Eight thousand Lamanites baptized
summary: Nephi and Lehi preach to the Lamanites with power and authority. Eight thousand Lamanites in Zarahemla and the surrounding area are baptized unto repentance and convinced of the wickedness of their ancestral traditions.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi preached to the Lamanites with power and authority and were given what to say.
Eight thousand Lamanites in Zarahemla and round about were baptized unto repentance and convinced of the wickedness of their fathers’ traditions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Lehi preach to a gathered audience; baptism is an appropriate visual representation of the reported event.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise location, arrangement, and manner of preaching and baptism.

narration.text: there were eight thousand of the Lamanites

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the converts individual names or biographies.

title: Journey toward the land of Nephi
summary: Nephi and Lehi set out for the land of Nephi, where a Lamanite army captures them and puts them in the prison where Ammon and his brethren had been held.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi proceeded to the land of Nephi.
A Lamanite army captured them and put them in the same prison where Ammon and his brethren had been held by Limhi’s servants.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Lehi can be shown in Lamanite custody at the prison.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and how the capture was carried out.

narration.text: they were taken by an army of the Lamanites and cast into prison

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon and his brethren are mentioned as having been imprisoned earlier; they are not present in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Ammon, his brethren, or Limhi’s servants in the prison now.

title: The prisoners approach
summary: After Nephi and Lehi have been imprisoned without food for many days, people enter the prison intending to kill them.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: After many days without food, people entered the prison to take Nephi and Lehi and slay them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The captors enter the prison while Nephi and Lehi are inside.
unspecified_visual_details: How many captors enter and what weapons, if any, they carry.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack or injury not narrated in this verse.

title: A pillar of fire surrounds Nephi and Lehi
summary: A pillar of fire encircles Nephi and Lehi without burning them. The Lamanites see it, take courage, but do not approach or touch the brothers.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi were encircled as if by fire, were not burned, and stood in its midst.
The Lamanites saw the pillar of fire and took courage.
The Lamanites did not dare touch or approach Nephi and Lehi and stood amazed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show Nephi and Lehi surrounded by fire, with the Lamanites keeping their distance.
unspecified_visual_details: The fire’s color, shape beyond a pillar, and the prison’s appearance.

narration.text: Nephi and Lehi were not burned

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the fire burning people or the prison.

title: Nephi and Lehi speak to the Lamanites
summary: Nephi and Lehi stand forth and tell the Lamanites not to fear, explaining that God has shown them they cannot kill the brothers.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi stood forth and spoke to the Lamanites, telling them not to fear and that God had shown they could not kill them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Lehi address the Lamanites from within the pillar of fire.
unspecified_visual_details: Gestures, expressions, and the captors’ positions.

spoken_dialogue.text: Fear not, for behold, it is God that has shown unto you this marvelous thing,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi and Lehi

prohibited_inventions: Do not add speech beyond the supplied words.

title: The prison shakes
summary: The earth shakes and the prison walls tremble without falling. A cloud of darkness overshadows the Lamanites and Nephite dissenters, bringing awful solemn fear.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The earth shook exceedingly and the prison walls shook as if about to fall, but did not; the prisoners included Lamanites and Nephite dissenters.
A cloud of darkness overshadowed them and awful solemn fear came upon them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prisoners are inside a trembling prison as darkness covers them.
unspecified_visual_details: The darkness’s visual density and the prisoners’ individual reactions.

narration.text: the walls of the prison did shake as if they were about to tumble to the earth

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the prison walls collapsing.

title: A voice calls them to repent
summary: A voice from above the cloud commands the prisoners to repent and stop trying to destroy God’s servants. Though mild and whisper-like, it is accompanied by another shaking of the earth and trembling walls; the darkness remains.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: A voice as if above the cloud told them to repent and stop trying to destroy God’s servants.
The voice was mild, not thunderous or tumultuous, and pierced to the soul.
The earth shook and the prison walls trembled again, while the cloud remained.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The voice is off-screen, coming from above the cloud.
unspecified_visual_details: The source or visible form of the voice.

spoken_dialogue.text: Repent ye, repent ye, and seek no more to destroy my servants whom I have sent unto you to declare good tidings.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The voice is heard but its speaker is not identified here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or angel.

title: The voice speaks again
summary: The voice again calls them to repent and stop trying to destroy God’s servants. The earth and prison shake; a third utterance contains words that cannot be spoken by man. The Lamanites cannot flee, held by darkness and fear.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The voice again called them to repent because the kingdom of heaven was at hand and to stop trying to destroy God’s servants; the earth and walls shook.
A third time the voice spoke marvelous words that cannot be uttered by man, and the walls and earth trembled.
The Lamanites could not flee because of the darkness and fear.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the prisoners immobilized in darkness as the prison shakes.
unspecified_visual_details: The content of the third utterance and the voice’s source.

spoken_dialogue.text: Repent ye, repent ye, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; and seek no more to destroy my servants.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The third utterance is expressly beyond human words and is not supplied as dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words of the third utterance or show the earth splitting.

title: The multitude turns and looks
summary: A Nephite by birth who had dissented from the church turns and sees Nephi and Lehi through a cloud of darkness. Their faces shine exceedingly, and they lift their eyes to heaven as if speaking to a being they behold. The man cries to the multitude to turn and look; they turn and see their faces.

explicit_facts.text: The man was a Nephite by birth who had once belonged to the church of God but had dissented.
He turned and saw the faces of Nephi and Lehi through the cloud of darkness; their faces shone exceedingly, even as the faces of angels.
Nephi and Lehi lifted their eyes to heaven and appeared to be talking or lifting their voices to a being they beheld.
The man cried to the multitude to turn and look. Power was given to them to do so, and they saw the faces of Nephi and Lehi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Frame the man's turn and the multitude's later turn as successive moments, not a single simultaneous action.
unspecified_visual_details: The man's appearance
The multitude's appearance and composition
The surrounding setting

narration.text: they did shine exceedingly, even as the faces of angels.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparison to angels does not describe angels appearing. The being Nephi and Lehi seemed to behold is not described as visible to the multitude.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man or identify the multitude beyond what these verses state.
Do not depict angels or give the being Nephi and Lehi seemed to behold an appearance.
Do not invent the words the man cried out.

title: Aminadab answers the multitude
summary: The Lamanites ask what the events mean and who the brothers are conversing with. Aminadab answers that they converse with angels of God.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites asked what the events meant and whom Nephi and Lehi were conversing with.
Aminadab said that they were conversing with angels of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites address Aminadab while looking toward Nephi and Lehi.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the angels; they are not explicitly described as visible here.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, what do all these things mean, and who is it with whom these men do converse?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lamanites

spoken_dialogue.text: They do converse with the angels of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Aminadab

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The existence or appearance of angels in this specific moment is reported by Aminadab.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict angels based only on Aminadab’s answer.

title: Aminadab tells them what to do
summary: The Lamanites ask Aminadab how the darkness can be removed. He tells them to repent and cry to the voice until they have faith in Christ, after which the darkness will be removed.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites asked Aminadab what they should do to have the cloud removed.
Aminadab told them to repent and cry to the voice until they had faith in Christ, taught to them by Alma, Amulek, and Zeezrom; then the cloud would be removed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aminadab speaks to the prisoners while the darkness remains.
unspecified_visual_details: The prisoners’ gestures and the darkness’s visual appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: You must repent, and cry unto the voice, even until ye shall have faith in Christ,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Aminadab

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma, Amulek, and Zeezrom are mentioned as past teachers, not present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Alma, Amulek, or Zeezrom in the prison.

title: The darkness disperses
summary: The prisoners cry to the voice, and the cloud of darkness disperses. Looking around, they see every soul encircled by a pillar of fire.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: They all began crying to the voice of the one who had shaken the earth, until the darkness dispersed.
After the cloud dispersed, they saw every soul encircled by a pillar of fire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the darkness clearing to reveal each person surrounded by fire.
unspecified_visual_details: The fire’s exact appearance and how the people cry out.

narration.text: they did cry even until the cloud of darkness was dispersed

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the fire harming anyone.

title: Fire and the Holy Spirit
summary: Nephi and Lehi stand amid the fire, unharmed along with the prison walls. The people are filled with joy; the Holy Spirit comes down from heaven into their hearts, and they speak marvelous words.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi were in the midst of the people, encircled by fire that harmed neither them nor the prison walls; they were filled with unspeakable joy.
The Holy Spirit of God came down from heaven and entered their hearts; they were filled as if with fire and could speak marvelous words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown within the pillars of fire; the Holy Spirit’s descent can be shown without inventing a bodily form.
unspecified_visual_details: The Holy Spirit’s visible form and the content of the marvelous words.

narration.text: the Holy Spirit of God did come down from heaven

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Being filled as if with fire describes the people; the text does not give the Holy Spirit a visible body.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words they spoke or a bodily appearance for the Holy Spirit.

title: A voice gives peace
summary: A pleasant, whisper-like voice speaks peace to the people because of their faith in the Beloved, who was from the foundation of the world.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: A pleasant voice, like a whisper, came to them.
The voice said peace was upon them because of their faith in the Well Beloved, who was from the foundation of the world.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The voice can be represented as off-screen over the people in the prison.
unspecified_visual_details: The voice’s source and whether it has any visible form.

spoken_dialogue.text: Peace, peace be unto you, because of your faith in my Well Beloved, who was from the foundation of the world.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified voice

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the voice’s speaker.

title: Angels minister to the people
summary: The people look upward and see the heavens open. Angels come down and minister to them. About three hundred people see and hear these things and are bidden not to marvel or doubt.
locations: Prison in the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The people looked upward, saw the heavens open, and angels came down out of heaven and ministered to them.
About three hundred souls saw and heard these things and were bidden not to marvel or doubt.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the heavens open above the prison as angels descend and minister to the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels’ appearance and the manner of their ministering.

narration.text: angels came down out of heaven and ministered unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angels’ appearance is not described; do not add distinguishing features.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent angel names or individual biographies.

title: Witnesses minister among the people
summary: Those who saw and heard the prison events go out and minister to people in the surrounding regions, declaring what they had heard and seen. Many Lamanites are convinced by the evidence they received.
locations: Regions around the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The witnesses went forth, ministered to the people in surrounding regions, and declared what they had heard and seen.
The greater part of the Lamanites were convinced because of the evidence they had received.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The witnesses can be shown sharing their experience with groups in the surrounding regions.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular places, audiences, and contents of their accounts.

narration.text: declaring throughout all the regions round about all the things which they had heard and seen

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This reports their ministry and its effect; no particular speech is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or identify individual witnesses.

title: Weapons Laid Down
summary: Those convinced laid down their weapons of war, hatred, and the tradition of their fathers. They yielded the lands of their possession to the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: As many as were convinced laid down their weapons of war, hatred, and the tradition of their fathers.
They yielded the lands of their possession to the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People laying down weapons of war may be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearance of the people and weapons.
The manner in which the lands were yielded.

narration.text: And as many as were convinced did lay down their weapons of war, and also their hatred and the tradition of their fathers.
And it came to pass that they did yield up unto the Nephites the lands of their possession.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Laying down hatred and tradition is not a separate literal physical action.
The verses do not describe how the lands were yielded.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent negotiations, a ceremony, named leaders, or specific land boundaries.
Do not depict the yielding of lands as occurring simultaneously with the laying down of weapons.
